blocks.heading: Polar Expeditions and Test-Range Science

items.text: These come up constantly in "travel science career" searches, and they deserve an honest, direct answer rather than being quietly left out.

India's Antarctic and Arctic research programme, run through the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), sends a genuinely small number of scientists a year, almost always PhD-level specialists in glaciology, atmospheric science, or polar oceanography, to stations like Maitri and Bharati.
Test-range science, flight-test and trial-campaign work at DRDO, ISRO, or HAL, involves real travel to test sites like Chandipur, Sriharikota, or Thumba during trial campaigns.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Polar expeditions and test-range science: the rare edge cases

items.text: Several of these tracks have more than one hard filter, not just one entrance exam.
Entry into GSI and ONGC as a geologist runs through a competitive recruitment or GATE-linked exam and interview.
Clearing the Wildlife Institute of India's entrance test for its postgraduate programme is genuinely competitive on its own.

blocks.heading: Four Questions Before You Chase This

items.text: A pay table cannot tell you whether fieldwork-heavy science genuinely fits your temperament, your finances, and your life stage.

These careers reward people who can genuinely tolerate weeks away from home comforts, rough accommodation, physical exertion, and unpredictable schedules, and who do not treat fieldwork as a temporary adventure phase before "settling down" into a desk.
If the pull is really the idea of travel photos, not the actual science being done at the site, that mismatch shows up fast in the first field season, not years later.

You are choosing between these fields mainly because "travel" sounds exciting

Travel here means remote camps, coastal field stations, forest postings, and short EIA site visits, not a scenic-photo career. Pick the underlying science first; the travel is a real but secondary feature of the job.
You are imagining polar expeditions or global assignments as a realistic entry-level outcome

NCPOR sends a handful of PhD-level scientists on Antarctic and Arctic missions a year. Nearly every geologist, marine biologist, wildlife researcher, and environmental scientist in India works entirely inside domestic postings.
You want a stable, predictable income and dislike project-to-project funding uncertainty

Wildlife and conservation fieldwork in particular runs on short-term, project-based funding for long stretches of a career. Government research posts are more stable, but the ladder to reach them is slow and exam-gated.
You are in, or planning, a family situation that needs consistent physical presence

Extended field seasons, research cruises, and remote postings genuinely strain relationships and parenting in ways worth discussing honestly with a partner or family before committing years of study to one of these tracks.
